_what_this_file_is: Per-jurisdiction rules for allocating a player's salary across the
states he works in. Roughly 41 states plus DC tax nonresident
athletes; the ones that do not are seeded verified below because a
state having no wage income tax is a structural fact rather than a
EVERYTHING ELSE IS status: unverified AND HAS NULL RATES, ON PURPOSE.
The brief's instruction was: do not invent these values, seed what
can be verified from primary sources, mark the rest unverified so the
UI can suppress them, because a wrong tax number is worse than a
missing one. That is what this file does.
What the tool still does with an unverified state: counts the duty
days, computes the allocation percentage, and puts both in the CPA
export. That is the laborious, error-prone part and it does not
depend on a rate. What it withholds is the dollar liability.
TO VERIFY A STATE: fill in top_marginal_rate / bracket_structure,
any duty_day_overrides that differ from config/tax/duty-day-rules.json,
reciprocity, resident-credit mechanics and filing threshold; record
where each came from in `source`; set status to 'verified'. The UI
picks it up with no code change.
allocation_formula: (duty days in jurisdiction / total duty days) * allocable income

AL.name: Alabama
AL.note: Rates and duty-day treatment NOT verified. The engine counts duty days and computes this state's allocation percentage, which is rate-independent and useful on its own, but it will not produce a liability estimate until someone fills in the rate structure and changes this status.

AK.name: Alaska
AK.note: No individual income tax on wages, so duty days here generate no state liability. Days are still counted: they sit in the denominator and therefore reduce every other state's share.
AK.source: Structural feature of the state's tax system, stable across years. Not a rate-table lookup.

CA-ON.name: Ontario, Canada
CA-ON.note: Toronto is a road series for every American League club and several National League ones. Days worked in Canada raise federal and provincial obligations and a treaty question, none of which this tool models. It is listed so the days are visible in the export and in the denominator rather than quietly disappearing. This one in particular is a conversation with a preparer, not a number to estimate.
